comment: Settings shown by Pipewire Simple Configurator. Each group appears on every page whose scope is listed in 'scopes'; a setting can narrow that with its own 'scopes'. Types: bool, int, float, enum, rate, ratelist, quantum, fraction, string, list. 'default' is the documented PipeWire/WirePlumber default and is only used when no config file and no running device report a value.

groups.title: Sample rates
groups.description: The graph is the clock that every output and input device and every application stream runs on. It is shared by playback and recording.

settings.label: Default rate
settings.help: Rate the graph runs at when no stream needs one of the other allowed rates.

settings.label: Allowed rates
settings.help: Rates the graph may switch to, so streams at these rates play without resampling. Only pick rates your devices support. Adding a rate here is the safe way to get high-resolution playback.

groups.title: Buffer size (quantum)
groups.description: Values are in samples at the default rate; the latency is shown next to each value. When the graph runs at another rate, PipeWire scales the default, minimum and maximum quantum with it (1024 at 48 kHz becomes 4096 at 192 kHz). The limit and floor are not scaled.

settings.label: Default quantum
settings.help: Buffer size used when no stream asks for anything else. Smaller means lower latency but more CPU load and a higher risk of crackling.

settings.label: Minimum quantum
settings.help: Smallest buffer size a stream may request.

settings.label: Maximum quantum
settings.help: Largest buffer size a stream may request.

settings.label: Quantum limit
settings.help: Hard upper limit for any buffer size, including forced ones, and the buffer space every node reserves. PipeWire accepts at most 65536. Applications size some of their own buffers from their own config, so this value is also written to client.conf, pipewire-pulse.conf and jack.conf.

settings.label: Quantum floor
settings.help: Hard lower limit for any buffer size, including forced ones.

settings.label: Round quantum to a power of two
settings.help: The graph quantum is rounded down to a power of two (960 runs as 512), which is more efficient for most processing. Turn off to use values such as 960 (exactly 20 ms at 48 kHz). Quanta forced with "Try now" are never rounded.

settings.label: Requested latency
settings.help: Buffer size a stream asks for when the application does not ask for one itself, written as samples / rate.

settings.label: Force graph rate
settings.help: Every playing stream forces the whole graph to this rate.
settings.warning: This pins the graph for every device, including Bluetooth headphones, and stops PipeWire from switching between the allowed rates. Prefer adding the rate to the allowed rates on the Graph page.

groups.title: Device format
groups.description: Leave these off to let the device follow the graph.

settings.label: Fixed rate
settings.help: Always open the device at this rate. PipeWire resamples when the graph runs at a different rate.

settings.label: Allowed rates
settings.help: Rates this device may be opened with. When the graph runs at another rate, PipeWire resamples to the nearest allowed one.

settings.label: Sample format
settings.help: Format the device is opened with. Only pick a format the hardware supports.

groups.title: Device buffering
groups.description: Mostly useful against crackling or dropouts on USB and HDMI devices.

settings.label: Period size
settings.help: Size of one hardware period. 0 lets PipeWire choose the smallest working size.

settings.label: Number of periods
settings.help: 0 uses as many periods as the device allows.

settings.label: Headroom
settings.help: Extra safety margin in the device buffer, for devices that report their position inaccurately. Raise it in steps of 256 if you hear crackling.

settings.label: Start delay
settings.help: Extra delay for devices that need time before they report correct positions.

settings.label: Ignore batch flag
settings.help: Ignore the ALSA batch flag to save one period of latency. Can cause dropouts on devices that really need it.

settings.label: Display name
settings.help: Name shown in sound settings and mixers.

settings.label: Default priority
settings.help: Devices with a higher value are preferred when WirePlumber picks the default device.

settings.label: Suspend after idle
settings.help: Close the device after it has been idle this long. 0 keeps it open, which avoids pops or a cut-off first second of sound, at the cost of a little power.

settings.label: Hide this device
settings.help: Do not create this device at all.

groups.title: Resampler
groups.description: Used when a stream or device runs at a different rate than the graph, and to correct clock drift between devices.

settings.label: Quality
settings.help: 0 is fastest, 14 is best and uses the most CPU.

settings.label: Filter window
settings.help: Window function used to build the resampling filter.

settings.label: Exp: A
settings.help: 0 picks a value that matches the quality level.

settings.label: Blackman: alpha
settings.help: 0 picks a value that matches the quality level.

settings.label: Kaiser: alpha
settings.help: 0 derives it from the stopband attenuation.

settings.label: Kaiser: stopband attenuation
settings.help: 0 picks a value that matches the quality level.

settings.label: Kaiser: transition bandwidth
settings.help: 0 picks a value that matches the quality level.

settings.label: Cutoff
settings.help: Filter cutoff as a fraction of the Nyquist frequency (half the sample rate). 0 picks a value that matches the quality level.

settings.label: Filter taps
settings.help: Filter length. 0 picks a value that matches the quality level.

settings.label: Prefill with silence
settings.help: Fill the resampler with silence when it starts, so the first samples are not lost.

settings.label: Disable resampling
settings.help: Turn the resampler off completely.
settings.warning: Streams or devices whose rate differs from the graph will then play at the wrong speed, and devices cannot correct clock drift. Bluetooth devices always need the resampler.

groups.title: Channel mixing
groups.description: How channels are mixed when a stream and a device have a different channel layout, for example stereo music on 5.1 speakers.

settings.label: Upmix
settings.help: Spread stereo to surround speakers.

settings.label: Upmix method
settings.help: How the extra channels are created when upmixing.

settings.label: Mix LFE into other channels
settings.help: Mix the subwoofer channel into the remaining channels when the device has no LFE output.

settings.label: Normalize
settings.help: Lower the volume when mixing so the sum cannot clip.

settings.label: LFE cutoff
settings.help: Low-pass filter for the generated LFE channel. 0 disables it.

settings.label: Center cutoff
settings.help: Low-pass filter for the generated center channel. 0 disables it.

settings.label: Rear delay
settings.help: Delay of the generated rear channels.

settings.label: Stereo widen
settings.help: Subtract part of the center from the front channels. 0 disables it.

settings.label: Hilbert taps
settings.help: Phase shift for the rear channels. 0 disables it.

settings.label: Lock volumes
settings.help: Ignore volume changes from applications.

settings.label: Disable channel mixing
settings.help: Turn channel mixing off completely. Channels are then passed through by position only.

groups.title: Dither
groups.description: Only matters when the output format has fewer bits than the 32 bit float used internally.

settings.label: Method
settings.help: Noise added before reducing the bit depth, to avoid quantization distortion.

settings.label: Extra noise bits
settings.help: Adds noise of this many bits, mainly for testing.

settings.label: Disable filter graphs
settings.help: Do not run filter graphs (EQ and other filters configured in PipeWire or WirePlumber) on these nodes.
settings.warning: This also turns off EQ and other filters configured as PipeWire filter graphs.

groups.title: PulseAudio buffers
groups.description: Buffer sizes for applications that use the PulseAudio API, written as samples / rate.

settings.label: Minimum request
settings.help: Smallest write a client may ask for.

settings.label: Default request
settings.help: Write size for clients that do not ask for one.

settings.label: Minimum fragment
settings.help: Smallest fragment size for recording streams.

settings.label: Default fragment
settings.help: Fragment size for recording streams that do not ask for one.

settings.label: Default target length
settings.help: Buffer length for playback streams that do not ask for one.

settings.label: Minimum quantum
settings.help: Smallest quantum a client can force on the graph.

settings.label: Pause after underrun
settings.help: Pause a stream that keeps underrunning for this long. 0 never pauses.

settings.label: Quirks
settings.help: Workarounds for applications that misbehave. Blocking microphone volume changes stops apps such as Discord or Chrome from changing your mic level.

settings.label: Allowed codecs
settings.help: Codecs offered to headphones. When not set, every codec your PipeWire build supports is allowed. Codecs your PipeWire build lacks are ignored.

settings.label: Enable SBC-XQ
settings.help: Higher-bitrate SBC. Works on most headphones but not all, so by default it is only enabled for known-good models.

settings.label: Codec sample rate
settings.help: Preferred rate when the headphones support several. This is chosen when the device connects, independently of the graph rate.

settings.label: Enabled roles
settings.default: [ a2dp_sink a2dp_source bap_sink bap_source hfp_hf hfp_ag ]
settings.help: Bluetooth profiles this computer offers. Removing the HFP roles disables the headset (microphone) profile.

settings.label: Enable mSBC
settings.help: Wideband speech codec for the headset profile. Enabled by default for known-good headsets.

settings.label: Hardware volume
settings.help: Let the headphones control the volume themselves. Turn off if volume jumps or is too quiet.

settings.label: Headset backend
settings.help: Which component handles the headset profile.

settings.label: Switch to headset profile for the microphone
settings.help: When an application starts recording, switch the headphones to the headset profile so the microphone works. This lowers playback quality until recording stops.

settings.label: LDAC quality
settings.help: High quality needs a strong Bluetooth signal and drops out more easily, especially near 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.

settings.label: AAC bitrate mode
settings.help: Variable bitrate gives better quality for the same bandwidth on most headphones.
